front: Which step of the derivation needs the Markov property?
back: Replacing $\mathbb{E}[G_{t+1}|s_t=s,a_t=a,s_{t+1}=s']$ by $V^\pi(s')$: the future depends only on $s'$.
$V=r_\pi+\gamma P_\pi V\Rightarrow V=(I-\gamma P_\pi)^{-1}r_\pi$; $P_\pi$ is $S\times S$, row-stochastic.

front: Why is the Bellman operator a contraction?
back: $\|TV-TW\|_\infty\le\gamma\|V-W\|_\infty$ because rows of $P$ are probability vectors (and $|\max x-\max y|\le\max|x-y|$ for the optimality operator).
Compute $V^\pi$ for a fixed policy by sweeping $V\leftarrow T^\pi V$ until the largest change is below a tolerance.
$\pi'(s)=\arg\max_a Q^\pi(s,a)$; the improvement theorem guarantees $V^{\pi'}\ge V^\pi$.
Alternate full evaluation and greedy improvement until the policy is stable; the result satisfies the optimality equation.
Repeat $V\leftarrow\max_a Q_V(s,a)$; extract the greedy policy at the end. One sweep merges evaluation and improvement.
Any interleaving of evaluation and improvement; the value and policy converge together to $V^*,\pi^*$.

front: Why study DP if it needs a known model?
back: It defines optimality, is the test oracle for model-free methods, and Q-learning/TD are sampled versions of its backups.

front: Cost comparison: linear solve vs sweeps
back: Solving $(I-\gamma P_\pi)V=r_\pi$ costs $O(S^3)$; one sweep costs $O(S^2A)$ (less for sparse $P$).
